Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types using Landsat 5 and 7 surface reflectance data from 2001, computing multiple vegetation and moisture indices (NDVI, SAVI, EVI, NDWI, etc.), merging them with elevation and slope derived from SRTM, and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on user-defined regions to produce a classified land cover map which is exported to Google Drive.

Task: Estimate daily actual evapotranspiration
Estimate daily actual evapotranspiration (ETa) using the SSEBop (SSEB with operational parameters) model. It processes satellite imagery (Landsat and Sentinel-2) to derive land surface temperature (Ts), vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI2), and emissivity. Meteorological data from GLDAS or Xavier datasets are used to compute reference evapotranspiration (ETr) and other forcing variables. A cold-edge temperature (Tc) is derived using a C-factor from historical or scene-based statistics, and the dT (temperature difference) is calculated either from precomputed climatology or physically modeled. The ET fraction (ETf) is computed as a function of Ts, Tc, and dT, then multiplied by ETr to yield ETa. Outputs include ETa, ETf, Ts, ETo, ETr, and intermediate meteorological and spectral layers, exported to Google Cloud Storage and visualized on the map.

Task: Classify land cover types
Classify land cover types in a region of interest using Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from 2021. It applies cloud masking via the QA60 band to remove cloudy pixels, then trains a CART (Classification and Regression Trees) classifier using manually labeled training points for five classes: Vegetation, Water, Agriculture, Urban Built-Up, and Bare Land. The classification is performed on reflectance bands B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, and B7 at 10–20 m resolution, resulting in a classified raster map with distinct color coding for each land cover type. The output includes a visualization of the true-color image, the classified map displayed over the study area, and an export of the classified raster to Google Drive clipped to the ROI.
